arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Jeffrey Fisher argued that the Confrontation Clause text and history support his position.
Fisher stated that the prosecution cannot introduce one person's statements through another.
Fisher cited the Melendez-Diaz decision to support the testimonial nature of lab reports.
The state's advocate argued that police interrogations differ from forensic report creation.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Sixth Amendment right to confront witnesses. the side that brought the case argues that only the analyst who created the report can testify. The state argues that any qualified analyst can present the findings.

The state wants the Court to allow any qualified analyst to present the forensic results.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that the Confrontation Clause bars one person from testifying about another person's testimonial statements.
The state argues that the report is not a product of structured interrogation and does not require the original creator.

paragraphs: This issue determines how states must present forensic evidence in criminal trials. It affects the resources required to prove scientific findings. It shapes the practical application of the right to confront witnesses.
